subject: DPA onboarding: access categorization & transfer exception clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Garcia <elena@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA onboarding: access categorization & transfer exception clarifications

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. As we move through the DPA annex and security questionnaire I have a few targeted clarifications that our legal and privacy teams need before we sign:

1) Access categorization: we classify data into Identifiers / Sensitive Health / Derived Embeddings / Telemetry. For each category please confirm where Redwood stores the raw/staged data, where it is tokenized/pseudonymized, and which roles (engineering, SRE, support) can access plaintext.

2) Cross-border transfer exceptions: our model ops team requests a narrow exception to allow transient transfer of pseudonymized payloads to US-hosted model optimization clusters. Can you describe the transfer escort/logging you use and whether you can commit to an entry in the DPA that limits that exception to <48 hours and excludes re-identification?

3) Subprocessor list & KMS custody: please confirm the list of subprocessors that will handle telemetry and model traces and indicate who holds KMS keys for production data encryption.

4) Evidence: we need an annotated dataflow diagram showing the custody boundary (where PII is held), the Kafka topics that contain tokens vs identifiers, and a sample of the access matrix (roles + justification).

I attached our initial SSQ (high level) — please respond inline or attach a short matrix. If easier, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Elena
Senior Privacy Manager
Clearpath Health
[Attachment: Clearpath_SSQ_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2025 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA onboarding: access categorization & transfer exception clarifications

Hi Elena — Jordan here from Infra/SRE. Quick answers and pointers below; see attached diagram for a visual: redwood-dataflow-v2.svg (link included).

1) Where data is stored / tokenized
- Identifiers: stored only in tenant-scoped persistent storage in the customer project (encrypted at rest). We tokenize on ingress at the API edge and drop raw identifiers from ephemeral workers.
- Sensitive Health: retained in encrypted S3 buckets in the region you select; access strictly gated to a small set of engineering roles for on-call ops and the CS remediation team.
- Derived Embeddings: stored in a vector index cluster (configurable region); these are hashed and not reversible to plaintext without the original context.
- Telemetry: aggregated telemetry is stored in a separate analytics namespace; raw request traces that include PII are redacted at the edge and only persisted if required by a support ticket (with audit).

2) Transfer escort / logging model
- Transfer escort = an automated transfer orchestration that: 1) creates a signed transfer manifest, 2) streams payloads over mTLS, 3) writes a transfer audit record (transfer_id, tenant_id, sha256(payload), ttl).
- Manifests and transfer logs are retained in our audit log system for 90 days by default (can be configured in Dedicated/Private).
- For your requested exception we can: (a) limit to pseudonymized payloads, (b) automatically redact known identifiers server-side, and (c) enforce a 48-hour TTL via the manifest.

3) Subprocessors & KMS
- Subprocessors that may see telemetry or traces: Cloud Storage Provider (US region), Managed DB vendor (separate), and a vector index provider for embeddings (configurable). Full current roster is linked in the diagram and in our subprocessor registry.
- KMS custody: Redwood holds the root key in a customer-isolated envelope; customers can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) — in BYOK mode the customer retains key custody and Redwood operates with a wrapped DEK.

4) Evidence & artifacts
- Annotated diagram: https://drive.google.com/redwood/dataflow/v2 (attached as redwood-dataflow-v2.svg).
- Access matrix (attached): redwood-dpa-access-matrix.xlsx — includes roles (engineering, infra-sre, support, cs-remediation), least-privilege justification and break-glass controls.

If you want concrete log samples (anonymized) we can produce a 1-day export with identifiers masked.

-Jordan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dataflow-v2.svg (svg)]

From: Elena Garcia <elena@clearpathhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA onboarding: access categorization & transfer exception clarifications

Jordan / Sofia — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we share with legal: 

- Transfer escort: can you confirm where the transfer audit records live (project/account) and who has read access to them? Our compliance team needs to see that logs cannot be modified and that log access is restricted to an audit role.

- 48-hour exception: legal wants explicit DPA language. Would Redwood accept a clause that: (a) limits transfers to pseudonymized payloads only, (b) requires an exported manifest with TTL enforcement, and (c) allows Clearpath to request a one-time manual verification (audited by Redwood) if re-identification is suspected?

- Subprocessor proof: procurement asked for an SSF export or a signed subprocessor attestation for the vendors handling vector indices. Please attach those artifacts.

Attaching our annotated SSQ with inline comments — I added comments on the KMS/BYOK and on retention.

Elena
[Attachment: Clearpath_SSQ_v1_annotated.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Garcia <elena@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA onboarding: access categorization & transfer exception clarifications

Elena — appreciate the quick review and the inline SSQ. Short answers and next steps below: 

- Transfer audit records: stored in a separate immutable audit project (audit-log-redwood) with write-once retention. Read access is restricted to the Audit role (auditors@redwood.com) and a scoped support/audit tooling account. We use WORM-backed storage for manifests and the logs are tamper-evident (SHA256 chain). We will provide a read-only IAM role for Clearpath auditors during onboarding, scope-limited and timeboxed.

- DPA language: Redwood can accept the three bullets you proposed with two minor edits (we will add "technical controls for pseudonymization" detail and include the manifest TTL enforcement). I will draft the clause and circulate by EOD Friday for your legal team.

- Subprocessor attestations: PrIyom will pull the signed attestation packages for the vector index vendors and the storage provider; we will deliver signed PDFs via the secure transfer link.

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
1) Fri 8 Aug — Redwood sends draft DPA exception clause + subprocessor attestations.
2) Mon 11 Aug — Clearpath legal provides redline or acceptance.
3) Wed 13 Aug — test transfer escort run (anonymized) and exchange audit-role access for 48 hours.

If those dates look good I’ll create a short DocuSign envelope for the DPA addendum after your legal confirmation.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Privacy & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
[Attachments to follow: subprocessor-attestations_2x.pdf]
